texts.preamble: Sadha Shivappa M L vs Devaraju B V on 30 January, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.4479/2023 Kabc0B0075952023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present : Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 30th Day of January-2025 M.V.C. No.4479/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Sadha Shivappa.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 24.06.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 24.06.2023 at about 06.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding electric bicycle from segehalli towards Kadugodi on left side of the said road slowly, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations, when reached near Belathur Junction, at that time one Tempo Traveller bearing Reg. No. KA-64-1855 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed from same direction and dashed against the petitioner's electric bicycle from behind. Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Axies Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and conveyance charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 47 years, the petitioner was working as vegetable and fruits vendor and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. The respondent No.2 appear through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tempo Traveller. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 152(2) and 158(6) of M. V. Act. Further, this respondent does not admit that the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler had valid driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of the accident. He also denied the age, Sadha Shivappa M L vs Devaraju B V on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176379124/ 2 occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.16 and also examined one Srinath.K as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 and 18 and closed their side.
texts.arguments: 15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,62,056/- towards medical expenses. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was vegetable and fruits vendor and earning Rs.30,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
